title: Introduce compact credential-fallback mesh and typed stream guard for cross-SDK ergonomics
author: Evelyn Cho
release_notes: Small API additions: optional resume_token in streaming envelopes, new RetryPolicy presets; cross-SDK version bumps (py 1.13.0, ts 2.8.1, go 1.5.4). Behavior: improved auth fallback ordering and stream resume semantics. No breaking changes expected for typical callers.
body:
Motivation: SDK users routinely wire multiple credential sources (env, file, metadata, delegated token) and expect a small, predictable fallback order plus clear hooks for advanced setups. Streaming callers ask for ergonomics around resume and a light guard that prevents callers from accidentally holding onto an unbounded async iterator when backpressure is present. This PR introduces a compact credential fallback mesh (CredMesh), a typed stream guard abstraction (TypedStreamGuard) exposed across Python/TS/Go SDKs, several retry-preset additions tuned for streaming and short-lived auth failures, and coordinated version bumps.

Summary of changes (high level): 1) auth: add CredMesh - a tiny ordered fallback registry that composes existing providers (Env, File, InstanceMetadata, Delegated) and exposes a single Acquire(ctx) API with fast-path caching and TTL-aware refresh. The mesh is intentionally small (~120 LOC per SDK) and pluggable for enterprise custom providers. 2) streaming: add TypedStreamGuard - a runtime guard that wraps async stream iterators/pull streams to enforce single-consumer semantics, automatic cancel-on-unsubscribe, and an optional "resume_token" handshake field on stream envelopes. Guard includes a light-weight heartbeat hook to surface early shutdowns to consumers. 3) retry: add two presets: "streaming_short" (aggressive fast-retries for transient auth/transport blips) and "streaming_stable" (more conservative). Wire presets into the SDK surface so callers can choose by name or pass the RetryPolicy object. 4) cross-SDK ergonomics: align function names and parameter order across py/ts/go for Acquire, Renew, and StreamGuard constructors; add shim adapters for older callsites to ease migration. 5) releases: bump sdk-python to 1.13.0, sdk-typescript to 2.8.1, sdk-go to 1.5.4; update changelogs and release artifacts.

Migration notes:
- To opt into resume semantics consumers should parse the new "resume_token" field from stream envelopes and pass it back via the resume header on reconnect.
- Applications using custom credential providers should implement the new Provider interface (single Acquire method); existing adapters are included to translate older interfaces.
- Default behavior preserves previous semantics; the CredMesh is only enabled when Constructed via the new NewCredMesh/NewCredMeshBuilder helpers.

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests added for mesh ordering, TTL refresh, and provider error aggregation across SDKs.
- End-to-end integration test in benchmark-lab that simulates metadata service flapping and asserts no token stomping under high concurrency.
- Manual smoke tests for streaming resume verified with a local server that injects mid-stream disconnects and validates resume_token roundtrip.
